# autopilot_app (Resource)

An app: a unit of consent. It owns repositories, names the senders it accepts work from with the kinds of task it accepts from each, and names the people who may start work for it themselves, with their GitHub logins.

AutoPilot takes a sender's task only when the app the task is billed to, and the app that owns each repository the task touches, accept that sender for that kind. An app may accept a sender that doesn't exist yet, so the app and the sender can be applied in either order.

Every argument but `name` is optional and sent only when set. Removing one from the configuration empties it at AutoPilot: an app without `accepts` accepts no sender. Narrowing or deleting an app takes effect at once: AutoPilot stops the queued and running tasks the app no longer accepts.

A repository belongs to the first app that claims it. AutoPilot can't tell which app should own one, so review an app's `repos` as you would its access.

`credential` and `when_seats_full` are the app's credential policy: what the model calls of the tasks billed to it run on. A change to either sends both.

`worker_image`, `worker_cpu` and `worker_memory` choose the worker the tasks billed to the app run in: its image, and the size of the AWS Fargate task it runs as. `worker_cpu` and `worker_memory` are one size, set together, and a change to either sends both.

An app with this name that already exists is not taken over, even when its values match: the create fails and says to import it. The one exception is a create whose earlier attempt went unanswered (a gateway's 502, say) before an identical app answered: that attempt may have made the app, and the provider can't tell, so it takes the app as its own. `create_before_destroy` doesn't fit an app: the name is its key.

Import by name: `terraform import autopilot_app.billing billing`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
locals {
  developers = ["first.developer@example.com", "second.developer@example.com"]
}

resource "autopilot_app" "billing" {
  name = "billing"

  # The repositories this app owns. A repository belongs to one app at most.
  repos = ["example-org/billing-api", "example-org/billing-web"]

  # The senders it accepts work from, and the kinds it accepts from each.
  accepts = [
    {
      sender = "tracker"
      kinds  = ["implement-work-item", "fix-error", "review-pr"]
      # Let the tracker's review-pr tasks approve or request changes.
      can_decide = true
      # Let GitHub's auto-merge be turned on for the pull requests the
      # tracker's tasks open, when a task asks for it. GitHub merges each one
      # once the repository allows auto-merge and its required checks and
      # reviews pass.
      can_auto_merge = true
    },
    {
      sender = "monitor"
      kinds  = ["fix-error"]
    },
    {
      # Pull request reviews the developers start from GitHub.
      sender = "autopilot-github"
      kinds  = ["review-pr"]
      # Let them approve or request changes. On a pull request that may be
      # the asker's own they still only comment, unless can_decide_own_pr
      # is set to true as well. That check goes by the pull request's author
      # alone, so read can_decide's caveats before turning this on.
      can_decide = true
    },
  ]

  # The people who may start work for this app themselves.
  developers = local.developers

  # Each developer's GitHub login, so a review they start from GitHub runs
  # in their name. Every developer here must be in developers too.
  github_logins = [
    { login = "example-first-dev", developer = "first.developer@example.com" },
    { login = "example-second-dev", developer = "second.developer@example.com" },
  ]

  # What its tasks' model calls run on: a Claude seat when one has room,
  # and Bedrock when every seat is full.
  credential      = "seat_first"
  when_seats_full = "fall_back"

  # The worker its tasks run in: the ruby image, on a bigger task than the
  # default of 2 vCPU and 8 GB.
  worker_image  = "ruby"
  worker_cpu    = 4096
  worker_memory = 16384
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The app's name, which is its key and the `billing.app` of the work it pays for: a lowercase letter or digit, then lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`, at most 64 characters. Changing it replaces the app: Terraform deletes the old one, which stops its queued and running work at once, then creates the new one.

### Optional

- `accepts` (Attributes Set) The senders this app accepts work from, each at most once, with the kinds of task it accepts from each. At most 20. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--accepts))
- `credential` (String) What the model calls of the tasks billed to this app run on: `bedrock` (Amazon Bedrock, billed per token) or `seat_first` (one of the organization's Claude seats, when one has room). Left out, the app has no policy of its own, and AutoPilot's default applies: `bedrock`. AutoPilot uses seats only while its seat mode is on; with it off, every task runs on Bedrock. Removing it from the configuration takes the app's own policy away. The credential is chosen when a task starts, so a change reaches only the tasks that start after it.
- `developers` (Set of String) The people who may start work for this app themselves, through AutoPilot's MCP server, or from GitHub with a login in `github_logins`: their sign-in logins, which are email addresses, written in lowercase ASCII (AutoPilot refuses anything else). At most 100.
- `github_logins` (Attributes Set) The GitHub logins of this app's developers, for pull request reviews started from GitHub: each pairs a GitHub login with one of `developers`, and a review started from GitHub by that login runs in that developer's name. This decides who can start reviews in a developer's name, so review each pair as you would `developers`. Every `developer` here must also be in `developers`, so take someone's logins out in the same change that takes them out of `developers`. A developer may have more than one login, and each login belongs to one developer. At most 100. It also decides which pull requests count as a developer's own, for reviews from the MCP and from GitHub alike (`can_decide_own_pr`): one whose author isn't among a developer's logins here reads as someone else's, unless that developer has no login here at all. So a missing, wrong or stale pair can let a review approve someone's own work: pair every login a developer uses. Keep it up to date when someone renames their GitHub account: the old login no longer matches them, their pull requests under the new login read as someone else's, and someone else may take the old login. Reviews from GitHub also need the app to accept the `autopilot-github` sender for `review-pr`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--github_logins))
- `repos` (Set of String) The repositories this app **owns**, as `owner/name`. A repository belongs to at most one app. AutoPilot matches them without regard to case, so no two may differ only in case. At most 50.
- `when_seats_full` (String) With `credential = "seat_first"`, what a task does when every seat is full: `wait` until one has room, or `fall_back` to Bedrock. Required with `seat_first`, and only allowed with it.
- `worker_cpu` (Number) The CPU of the AWS Fargate task each of this app's tasks runs in, in CPU units, 1024 to a vCPU: `256`, `512`, `1024`, `2048` or `4096`. Set together with `worker_memory`. Left out with it, a task gets AutoPilot's default size, 2 vCPU and 8 GB, and removing both from the configuration takes the app back to it. A bigger task counts against AutoPilot's limits on running tasks and daily spend like any other. The size is chosen when a task starts, so a change reaches only the tasks that start after it.
- `worker_image` (String) The worker image the tasks billed to this app run in: `node`, `ruby`, `python` or `go`. Each is the same worker with that language's tools; `ruby` has Node too, for Rails assets. Choose the app's main language. Left out, the app's tasks run in `node`, and removing it from the configuration takes the app back to `node`. The image is chosen when a task starts, so a change reaches only the tasks that start after it.
- `worker_memory` (Number) The memory of that Fargate task, in MiB, at most 16 GB: one that Fargate allows with `worker_cpu`, which is `512`, `1024` or `2048` with `256`; `1024` to `4096` with `512`; `2048` to `8192` with `1024`; `4096` to `16384` with `2048`; `8192` to `16384` with `4096`; each range in steps of `1024`. Set together with `worker_cpu`.

### Read-Only

- `lock_version` (Number) The record's version, which AutoPilot raises on every change. Sent as `If-Match` on updates and deletes.

<a id="nestedatt--accepts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `accepts`

Required:

- `kinds` (Set of String) The kinds of task accepted from that sender, such as `implement-work-item` or `review-pr`. At least one.
- `sender` (String) The sender's name. It need not exist yet.

Optional:

- `can_auto_merge` (Boolean) Whether GitHub's auto-merge may be turned on for the pull requests that sender's `implement-work-item` and `fix-error` tasks open on this app's repositories, when the task asks for it. AutoPilot never merges: GitHub merges each pull request once the repository's own settings and ruleset allow it, which means the repository allows auto-merge and its required checks and reviews pass. Off, a person merges. Only with `implement-work-item` or `fix-error` in `kinds`. Off unless set: leaving it out is the same as `false`. Turning it off, or removing the entry or the app, leaves auto-merge on for a pull request that already has it, and GitHub still merges that pull request: turn auto-merge off on the pull request in GitHub.
- `can_decide` (Boolean) Whether that sender's `review-pr` tasks may approve or request changes on this app's repositories, which can count as a required review. Only with `review-pr` in `kinds`. For `autopilot-mcp` and `autopilot-github`, whose reviews run for the person who asked, a review of a pull request that may be that person's own only comments, unless `can_decide_own_pr` is set too. That check goes by the pull request's author alone, so it doesn't stop a developer who pushes their own commits onto someone else's pull request, or a bot's, and then asks: the review may approve their code. GitHub's "require approval of the most recent reviewable push" doesn't stop that either, since AutoPilot isn't the pusher, and GitHub keeps an approval through later pushes unless the branch dismisses stale approvals. On a repository where one approval alone lets a pull request merge, keep that in mind before turning this on. Defaults to `false`.
- `can_decide_own_pr` (Boolean) Whether, with `can_decide`, a review that sender makes for a person may also approve or request changes on a pull request that may be that person's own. Off, such a review only comments. Only for `autopilot-mcp` and `autopilot-github`, whose reviews run for a person (the one who asked on AutoPilot's MCP server, or the developer who asked on GitHub, with the label or the command), and only with `can_decide = true`. A pull request may be the asker's own when its author is a GitHub login that `github_logins` pairs with them, compared without regard to case, or when AutoPilot can't tell: GitHub names no author, or `github_logins` pairs no login with them. So with this off, a review decides only for an asker who has a login in `github_logins`, and only on a pull request whose author isn't one of their logins there. An author no login is paired with reads as someone else's, even when it is another account of the asker's, so pair every login a developer uses. It goes by the author alone, which leaves open what `can_decide` describes: commits pushed onto someone else's pull request. Turning it on lets a developer get an approval of their own pull request that can count as a required review, so set it only where that is acceptable. Off unless set: leaving it out is the same as `false`. When it is turned off, a deciding review of what may be the asker's own pull request that is still queued or running is refused or stopped; ask for the review again.


<a id="nestedatt--github_logins"></a>
### Nested Schema for `github_logins`

Required:

- `developer` (String) The developer that login belongs to: their sign-in login, an email address in lowercase ASCII, as it is written in `developers`.
- `login` (String) A GitHub login, written in lowercase (AutoPilot refuses uppercase): a letter or digit, then letters, digits, `-` and `_`, at most 39 characters.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an app by its name.
terraform import autopilot_app.billing billing
```
